therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: receptor antagonism / type I interferon receptor blockade
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: suppression of type I interferon signaling and downstream innate immune activation
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: adult patients with active systemic lupus erythematosus

results.target_engagement_evidence: IFN test-high subgroup analysis confirms interferon pathway engagement; BICLA response rate difference 17.3 pp in IFN-high subgroup
biomarker_changes: IFN test-high subgroup showed similar or greater BICLA benefit (MD 17.3, 95% CI 6.5–28.2, p=0.0022)
subgroup_findings: IFN test-high subgroup: BICLA response MD 17.3 pp (95% CI 6.5–28.2), p=0.0022
OCS reduction subgroup (baseline OCS ≥10 mg/day): maintained OCS ≤7.5 mg/day MD 21.2 pp (95% CI 6.8–35.7), p=0.0135
CLASI subgroup (baseline CLASI ≥10): ≥50% reduction at Week 12 MD 24.0 pp (95% CI 4.3–43.6), p=0.0392
Joint count subgroup (≥6 swollen and ≥6 tender joints): ≥50% reduction MD 4.7 pp (95% CI -10.6–20.0), p=0.5469 (not significant)
Annualized flare rate ratio 0.67 (95% CI 0.48–0.94), p=0.0809 (not significant at conventional threshold)
safety_signals: 162/180 anifrolumab vs 154/182 placebo participants had ≥1 AE
29/180 anifrolumab vs 20/182 placebo participants had ≥1 AESI (including serious infections, herpes zoster, opportunistic infections, malignancy, MACE)

Serious AEs included acute coronary syndrome and Chilaiditi's syndrome in anifrolumab arm; anaemia, atrial flutter, cardiac failure, haematemesis, intra-abdominal haematoma, oesophageal stenosis, influenza-like illness, cholecystitis in placebo arm

context.duration: 52 weeks treatment with up to 60 weeks total follow-up
